oneLiner: The broadest semiconductor equipment franchise riding a record AI-driven WFE cycle into tonight's Q3 print, re-rated from a ~20x cyclical to a ~36x forward secular growth story.
thesis: AI capex is inflecting AMAT's growth. Management raised its calendar-2026 semiconductor equipment growth outlook to 30%+ (from 20%+ in February), with advanced packaging revenue guided to grow 50%+.
Guidance implies a step-change. The Q3 FY26 guide of $8.95B came in roughly $860M above the then-consensus $8.09B, with EPS guided to $3.36 vs $2.88 expected.

Leverage to GAA and HBM. Materials-engineering intensity rises with gate-all-around transistors, backside power, and HBM stacking; Q2 DRAM systems revenue hit a record $1.7B (+18% YoY), and EPIC partnerships span TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron.
Services compound quietly. AGS grew 17% YoY to $1.665B in Q2 FY26 with 29.2% operating margin, a recurring-revenue ballast on a massive installed base.
Industry tailwind has legs. SEMI forecasts WFE up ~23% to ~$143.9B in 2026 and up a further ~22% in 2027.

latestProse: Q2 FY26 (ended Apr 26, 2026) revenue was a record $7.91B, +11% YoY, with non-GAAP gross margin at 50.0%, operating margin 32.1%, and record non-GAAP EPS of $2.86 (+20%); GAAP EPS of $3.51 was inflated by a tax benefit. Semiconductor Systems did $5.965B (foundry/logic 67%, DRAM 29%, flash 4% of systems), AGS $1.665B (+17%), Display $280M. The disclosure that mattered: Dickerson raised the CY26 equipment growth outlook to 30%+, while free cash flow collapsed 80% to $210M as AMAT built inventory ahead of the ramp.
guidanceProse: Q3 FY26 guidance: revenue $8.95B plus or minus $500M and non-GAAP EPS $3.36 plus or minus $0.20, far above pre-guide consensus ($8.09B / $2.88). Management expects CY26 semi equipment growth of 30%+ and packaging growth of 50%+, with China and global ICAPS flat to slightly higher. The headline debate into the Aug 13 print: whether Q4 guidance confirms sustained acceleration into CY27, and whether China (27% of sales) stays insulated after the suspended BIS affiliates rule (once flagged as a ~$600-710M FY26 hit) and the pending MATCH Act.

guide.label: Q3 FY26 revenue guide
guide.sub: ~$860M above consensus at guide; EPS $3.36; results Aug 13, 2026

segments: Semiconductor Systems: $5.965B, ~75% of Q2 FY26 revenue (foundry/logic 67%, DRAM 29%, flash 4% of segment)
Applied Global Services: $1.665B, ~21% of revenue, +17% YoY
Display/Other: $280M, ~4%; by region: Taiwan 27%, China 27%, Korea 20%
competitive: Lam Research: closest rival in deposition/etch, heavier memory/NAND mix
ASML: litho monopoly captures a growing WFE share; complementary rather than head-on
KLA: process-control leader; Tokyo Electron competes across deposition/etch/clean
AMAT is the largest process-equipment maker by revenue with the broadest portfolio
In advanced packaging, Besi/ASMPT compete in bonding; AMAT is acquiring ASMPT NEXX ($120M, May 2026)
moat: Breadth is the moat: AMAT touches more materials-engineering steps than any rival, and integrated platforms plus co-optimized process flows raise switching costs at GAA/backside-power/HBM inflections. A massive installed base feeds AGS recurring revenue at 29% operating margins, and the EPIC Center embeds AMAT in customers' next-node R&D.
risks: This is still a cyclical. WFE booms invert; SEMI's own 2027-28 deceleration path and any AI capex digestion would compress both estimates and the multiple.
China/export-control overhang. China is 27% of sales; the $252.5M BIS penalty is settled, but the suspended affiliates rule could return and the MATCH Act would restrict DUV servicing.
Valuation reset risk. ~51x trailing earnings is a decade-high multiple for AMAT, roughly 160% above its historical average.
Cash conversion deteriorated. FCF fell 80% YoY on inventory build; if orders slip, working capital unwinds painfully.
Customer concentration. Spending hinges on a handful of buyers (TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron); a single capex pause is material.
NAND and ICAPS are flat. Flash is just 4% of systems revenue, so growth rests narrowly on leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, and packaging.
catalysts: Aug 13, 2026: Q3 FY26 results and Q4 guide
Nov 2026: Q4 FY26 results with initial CY2027 commentary
H2 2026: MATCH Act progress; any reinstatement of the BIS affiliates rule
Late 2026: SEMI year-end WFE forecast update (2027 currently seen +~22%)
pricedIn: At $548.15 (Aug 12 close, +4.3% into earnings; ~$435B market cap), AMAT trades at ~51.6x trailing and ~35.8x forward earnings - a record trailing multiple versus a historical average near 20x - yet sits ~26% below its July peak of $739.67. Consensus target is ~$633 (Strong Buy). The market has re-rated AMAT from cyclical to AI-secular; the debate is whether 30%+ CY26 growth extends into CY27 (SEMI says WFE +~22%) or marks a cycle peak with China risk attached.

scenarios.bear: Q4 guidance disappoints or CY27 WFE flattens as AI capex digests; China restrictions return, clipping the 27% China mix. EPS estimates stall and the multiple mean-reverts toward mid-20s; stock retraces toward $380-420.
scenarios.base: Q3 lands near the $8.95B guide with EPS ~$3.36, Q4 confirms momentum, and FY26 finishes with equipment growth of 30%+. The stock recovers toward the ~$633 consensus target as CY27 WFE growth gets penciled in.
scenarios.bull: Beat-and-raise plus a strong CY27 WFE outlook (leading-edge logic, HBM/DRAM, packaging +50% compounding) drives estimates toward the bullish targets; stock retests the $700-740 highs.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: TTM FCF is artificially depressed (down 80%) by a deliberate pre-ramp inventory build, which would make an FCF-DCF read as far more expensive than the business is.
